blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Nobody would see the settlement worker fail or not run) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back until Paylane has proven itself in production: keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (provider selected from the environment) for at least one release cycle, and do not close the Stripe account until that period ends and a rollback criterion is met. State in the design how an operator switches back and who decides. Add the corresponding task to tasks.md.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Decide in the design how a failed or missed run is seen: an alert when the CronJob fails or has not completed successfully by a deadline (e.g. last-success timestamp metric or a heartbeat), a structured log at start and end with the run date and counts (fetched, matched, unmatched), and a way to re-run a given day safely. Add a task for it in tasks.md.
findings.title: Nobody would see the settlement worker fail or not run
